title: Rate-limiter neutralization for replayed output fragments and idempotent crediting
creator: Ava Patel
description:
Problem summary:

We observe clients that reconnect or experience retransmits receiving duplicated output fragments which trigger downstream rate-limiter and quota handlers, causing: double token debits, unexpected throttling, and temporary client-level bans. This is most visible for long-running streaming sessions where the client resumes and server resends recent fragments for resume semantics.

This ticket implements a targeted neutralization strategy in the rate-limiter and metering pipeline to avoid penalizing clients for intentionally replayed fragments while preserving protections against abuse (replay floods). The approach must be robust across midstream model switches, compressed multipart payloads, and attachments.
technical_design:
Key ideas and components:

1) Session-scoped fragment idempotency window:
   - Each streaming session will include a monotonic fragment sequence number and optional fragment-level id (client-provided or server-assigned).
   - Rate-limiter will maintain a short-lived per-session dedupe cache (sliding window, TTL ~120s) keyed by (session_id, fragment_id or seq). If a fragment is seen twice within the window, credits are ignored for the duplicate.

2) Provisional credits and finalization handshake:
   - Metering will provisionally allocate token credits for newly observed fragments but mark them as "provisional" in the write-ahead ledger. Finalization occurs on a terminal ACK or stable watermark. Replayed fragments within the provisional window will be reconciled to avoid double-charge.

3) Replay-safe rate-limit counters:
   - Token-bucket counters are updated only once per unique fragment. We will track the last-applied-seq per session in an atomic, append-only store to allow idempotent updates across process restarts.

4) Abuse protections and heuristics:
   - If replay frequency or unique fragment volume exceeds thresholds (e.g., >200 fragments/min or >10MB/min of replayed data), system classifies as potential abuse and falls back to standard rate-limiter behavior (no neutralization) and emits a security_alert metric.

5) Cross-cutting concerns:
   - For model handoffs (midstream model switch) we will map fragment ids across variants using canonical session metadata; if mapping unavailable, fall back to conservative crediting and emit diagnostic traces.
   - Attachments and compressed payloads contribute to an additional checksum key to avoid false dedupes when payload sizes differ but seq matches.

Implementation notes:
- Add a lightweight in-memory LRU per-replica dedupe cache (bounded memory) with periodic compaction and a backing Redis/kv checkpoint for long sessions.
- Extend metering ledger schema to support provisional=true and finalization_tx_id fields (note: store schema change handled in a separate migration PR).
- Expose new metrics: replay_dedup_rate, provisional_credits_pending, replay_abuse_flag_count.
testing_plan:
Unit tests:
- Dedup cache correctness (insert/evict/window semantics).
- Provisional credit lifecycle (create, reconcile, finalize, duplicate replay).

Integration tests:
- Simulate session resume: send fragments 1..N, disconnect, resend N-5..N, verify no double charge.
- Model switch: generate fragments framed with a model-handoff marker, verify fallback behavior and metrics.
- Abuse scenario: flood resends; verify neutralization disabled and alert emitted.

Load tests:
- Run 1000 concurrent streaming sessions with intermittent reconnects and validate per-session bucket fairness and overall throughput impact (<5% overhead).

Monitoring and verification:
- Dashboard that correlates session IDs, provisional credits, finalization latency, and charge-rate before/after change.
- Synthetic canary traffic that intentionally replays fragments to validate expected neutralization and thresholds.
acceptance_criteria: No duplicated token debits for replayed fragments in the integration harness (existing flaky tests converted to deterministic).
Rate-limiter CPU and memory overhead increases <= 8% under canary load with dedupe cache enabled.
Metrics emitted: replay_dedup_rate, provisional_credits_pending, replay_abuse_flag_count are populated and visible in console dashboards.
Fallback triggers correctly under replay-abuse load and results in security_alert metric.
Rollout plan validated in staging and one production shard; rollback path defined.
rollout_plan:
1) Feature flag gated implementation (config: metering.replay_neutralization = off by default).
2) Dark launch: enable on 1% traffic with metrics only (no neutralization) for 48h.
3) Canary enable on 1 prod shard with neutralization for 72h, monitor metrics and error rates.
4) Ramp incrementally to 25% -> 50% -> 100% over 7 days if no regression.
5) If replay_abuse_flag_count > 0.5% of sessions or provisional_credits_pending grows unbounded, immediately rollback to previous flag state.
notes:
Trade-offs considered:
- Stronger consistency (global dedupe store) would make neutralization bulletproof but significantly higher latency and cost; chosen design favors per-session bounded caches with conservative fallbacks.
- Schema change for ledger finalization deferred to a separate migration to keep this PR smaller; provisional fields will be appended in a backward-compatible manner.

Open questions:
- TTL for dedupe cache (default 120s) may need tuning per workload; propose an SLO-based experiment.
- Exact abuse thresholds to be finalized with SRE input.
